lenses.verdict: LENS 1 (Core UI fidelity), verdict FAIL with 5 MATERIAL findings. The successor at 516328c fixes the parallel design system from 8b06da5 at the token level. Color tokens, Inter Tight and JetBrains Mono, container-x max widths and gutters at every Core breakpoint, the 69px sticky header, the desktop nav labels and order, and the 4px black/outlined button geometry (52/60/64 at <768/768/1024) all match c0e25c73. The 1440 and 1280 header rows now look like production. But the preview still does not faithfully mirror production in five ways an approver would notice. (1) The Xenios mark renders invisibly everywhere: a white PNG is used as an , whereas Core draws it as a currentColor mask. That covers the header at all widths, the footer, and both columns of decision A. (2) The mobile and tablet header is effectively inverted. Core always shows Sign In, Start Care and Menu and hides the brand name below 520px. The preview hides Sign In at 700px and below and Start Care at 374px and below, shows the "Xenios" name, and moves the condensed nav from 1024 to 1160. (3) The heading ladder is one tier below Core (page h1 51.2px against Core's 76px; section h2 35px against 51.2px), and the clamp min/max values were changed (mobile h1 34px and 30px against Core's 32px). (4) Copy and page structure written for the preview replace Core's on Home, Care and Account/Status. These pages carry eyebrows claiming "Core-converged", "source-faithful shell" and "Current Core route families", with no PROPOSED label and no matching founder decision. (5) The "CURRENT CORE" card in decision D is rebuilt in the preview's own card layout, including a primary action on the held card that Core deliberately never renders. The drift matrix overstates fidelity for the header, footer, card radius and grid. The remaining drift is MINOR.

findings.area: Header/footer brand mark; decision A
findings.evidence: Preview index.html:28 and :71, plus preview.js:253 (decision A demo), render . preview.css:250-254 styles it as a plain image. The PNG has 37,078 opaque pixels and every one is in the 224-255 RGB bucket, i.e. white. Core index.css:226-235 (.wordmark-mark) instead tints that file through a CSS mask with background-color: currentColor (black), used at Navbar.tsx:110 and Footer.tsx:20. Pixel scan: in core-home-desktop-1440.png the mark shows dark pixels at x128-159, y26-41. In the same box of corrected-preview/home-desktop-1440.png (x100-160, y55-125) there are only 5 dark pixels, all on the edge of the 'X' in 'Xenios'. In home-mobile-390.png the header row (y148-204, x0-67) has 0 dark pixels, and 'Xenios' starts at x=68, after an empty 34px slot. Crop ui_conv_crops/lens1/brand_zoom_1440.png shows Core with the mark and the preview without it. founder-decisions-desktop-1440.png at about y1170-1130/0.75 (crop decisions_1440_0.png, decision A panels) shows bare 'Xenios' and 'Xenios Health' with a blank left gap. Yet FOUNDER_UI_DECISION_PACKET section A says 'Current Core: mark plus Xenios' and 'Proposed: mark plus Xenios Health'.
findings.claim: The Core mark is invisible on white across the preview: the global header at all 10 widths, the footer (only faintly visible on the gray footer), and both sides of decision A. An approver judging the header brand lockup never sees the current or proposed lockup as it would render in production.
findings.fix: Render the mark as Core does: <span class="wordmark-mark"> with background-color: currentColor and a mask on the same PNG. Or ship a dark variant of the asset. Re-capture header, footer and decision A at all widths.

The preview has .clarity-header-link{display:none} at max-width 700 (preview.css:1496-1498), .clarity-header-care.btn{display:none} at max-width 374 (1505-1508), and .clarity-brand-name at 19px (1492-1494). Probe header text: 430/390/375 'Xenios Start Care Menu'; 360/320 'Xenios Menu'. The condensed nav appears at min-width 1160 (preview.css:1436-1440), whereas Core shows it at 1024 (index.css:1477). Probe at 1024: 'Xenios Sign In Start Care Menu', with no For Individuals, For Practices, Partners or How It Works (crop hdr_1024_834.png). The footer also shows 'Xenios' on mobile (home-mobile-390.png bottom 500px, crop footer_mobile_390.png), but UI_CONVERGENCE_DRIFT_MATRIX rows 'Header actions' ('Sign In, rectangular Start Care, and Menu behavior at Core breakpoints') and 'Footer' ('Mobile footer name leak remains documented, not silently fixed') say otherwise.
findings.claim: The phone and tablet header does not show current production. Core phones show no brand name, only the mark, plus Sign In and Start Care. The preview shows the name (with an invisible mark) and drops Sign In below 701px and Start Care below 375px; at 1024 it drops the four primary links. This is the surface where decision A's brand string would appear on phones, so the current-state baseline for A is misrepresented. Two claims in the drift matrix are false.
findings.fix: Port Core's rules exactly: no display:none on .clarity-header-link or .clarity-header-care; at max-width 519 apply Core's padding/font reductions and the visually-hidden brand name; condensed nav at 1024. Correct the two drift-matrix rows, and either show the Core mobile lockup as the current state for decision A or label any departure as proposed.

findings.area: Typography scale per page type
findings.evidence: Core PublicPage h1 uses display-l (primitives.tsx:52) and ContentSection h2 uses display-m (primitives.tsx:81). Receipt (27a core-capture-receipt.json): /products, /status, /research, /quality, /support and /partners h1 are 76px/800 at 1440 and 32px at 390; /care is 51.2px/28px (CarePublicPages.tsx:76, display-m). The preview maps .page-hero h1 to display-m (preview.css:428-436) and .section-heading h2 / .comparison-section h2 to display-s (438-445). Probe at 1440: products, featured, cards, details, held, quote, coming, journeys and decisions h1 all measure 51.2px, against Core /products and /status at 76px; section h2 computes to 35.04px against Core's 51.2px. The tokens themselves were retuned: display-l is clamp(34px, 5vw + 0.25rem, 88px) against Core's clamp(32px, ..., 96px) (preview.css:419-426 vs index.css:127-133); display-m is clamp(30px, ..., 60px) against clamp(28px, ..., 64px); display-s is 25/46 against 24/48. Probe at 430 and below: home h1 34px against Core 32px; every other page h1 30px against Core 32px (display-l) or 28px (display-m). Visible in products_hero_1440.png ('Research products' 76px vs 'Browse exact identities...' 51px) and status_side_1440.png. Meanwhile the home lead (preview.js:93) claims it 'uses the dominant current Xenios public shell, typography...'.
findings.claim: Ten of the 12 preview surfaces put page h1 and section h2 one tier below Core's dominant public hierarchy, and mobile sizes match no Core treatment. Approvers see a lighter heading hierarchy than production, which also changes how product images read against the copy in decisions D and E. The four-H1 inconsistency is recorded, but the preview chose the minority Care/sign-in tier as its baseline and altered the clamps.
findings.fix: Copy Core's .display-l/.display-m/.display-s/.h3 declarations verbatim. Use display-l for page-hero h1 and display-m for section h2, matching PublicPage and ContentSection. Keep display-m only on the Care view, mirroring Core /care. Re-capture.

findings.area: Homepage and page copy/structure (Home, Care, Account/Status, Products)
findings.evidence: Home: preview.js:91-92 sets the eyebrow 'Private Core-converged prototype' and the h1 'Clear pathways for research and care.'. Core Home.tsx:43-44 has 'CARE · RESEARCH PRODUCTS · PRACTICES' and 'Care and research products, clearly separated.'. Core's home sections (Home.tsx:48-108: 6-card audience grid, PathwayTiles, How Care works, How research orders work, For Practices, Partners, Quality, FAQ, dark CTA row) are all absent. The preview replaces them with a 426/424/423/0 accounting strip, a featured image grid, a dark 'Identity is not commerce authority' band and a calibration sheet (home_hero_1440.png; home-desktop-1440.png y0-5617). Care: preview.js:229 eyebrow 'Care · source-faithful shell' with h1 'Care begins with licensed review.', against Core 'Start Care with a short request.' (CarePublicPages.tsx:104). The Care tab row, current-status card, 'How Care works', 'What Care is not', 'This site is not emergency care' and the footer '911' line are missing (care_side_1440.png). Account/status: preview.js:239 eyebrow 'Current Core route families' with lead 'mirror current Core hierarchy and terminology', but it shows a reference-only 'Check status' plus an inline timeline and account rows. Core /status (pages.tsx:719, 748-750) requires reference + email and 'Send secure status link', with h1 'Check order status' (status_side_1440.png). Products: h1 'Browse exact identities and governed states.' and a 423-card grid, against Core's 'Research products' gateway with 'Browse Research Catalog' / 'How ordering works' (products_hero_1440.png). Products at least labels its media as proposed; none of the copy or structure changes are labelled PROPOSED, and none appear in FOUNDER_UI_DECISION_PACKET A-E or the drift matrix (grep for home, headline or copy finds nothing).
findings.claim: Copy and page structure written for the preview silently replace Core on Home, Care and Account/Status, under eyebrows that assert Core fidelity. An approver cannot tell that production says 'Care and research products, clearly separated.' or uses a secure-link status flow. Because these changes sit outside decisions A-E, they could be carried into implementation without any decision.
findings.fix: For surfaces presented as current Core, reproduce Core's h1, eyebrow, lead, CTAs and section order verbatim (synthetic data allowed), and put proposals in clearly labelled PROPOSED blocks. Otherwise relabel those views as preview-authored scaffolding rather than 'Core-converged' or 'source-faithful'. If new home or Care copy or structure is intended, add it to the decision packet as an explicit decision.

findings.area: Cards: the 'CURRENT CORE' card in the decision D comparison
findings.evidence: preview.js:52-63 (currentPolicyCard) is labelled 'Current Core · text-only public / Early Access policy'. It reuses the preview card layout: family mono label plus pill status badge, preview h3 (700 weight, 20-29px), specification, a Category/Price state fact grid, and a full-width card-cta.primary (52-64px) with labels 'View product', 'Review Care pathway', 'View hold details' and 'Request a quote'. Core's EarlyAccessProductCard.tsx:196-310 is a compact `card ... p-4` with category mono-label, name in body-m font-medium (line 213), strength, description, '$X per unit' or 'Not available to order', a quantity selector, and availability copy ('Available to order' / 'Temporarily unavailable'). Its only action is 'Select' or 'Request availability', and the held state renders NO action control (lines 257 and 300 are gated on `sellable`). The held pair in product-card-comparison-desktop-1440.text.txt:105-126 shows 'FORMULATION HELD ... View hold details' as a black primary CTA on the CURRENT CORE card. The vocabulary 'Research access' and 'Formulation held' is also not Core's card vocabulary.
findings.claim: The left-hand 'current' card in decision D is not current Core. It is the proposed card with the image removed. For the held state it shows a primary action that Core explicitly refuses to render. Holding the layout constant is a legitimate experimental design, but the 'CURRENT CORE' label misrepresents production card anatomy and held-state behaviour to the approver.
findings.fix: Either render the CURRENT CORE side with Core's actual EarlyAccessProductCard anatomy and states (no action on held), or relabel it 'Proposed anatomy · no-image variant' and place a real Core card capture beside it (for example core-synthetic-catalog-order-request-cards or the member catalog capture).
